articles.title: Comparing Bristow and Latarjet procedures for anterior shoulder instability in competitive rugby players: a unique within-subject clinical analysis.
articles.authors: Hirose T, Tanaka M, Nakai H, Kotani Y, Kuratani K, Sahara W, et al.
articles.population: Competitive rugby players with anterior shoulder instability requiring bilateral coracoid transfer surgery
articles.outcomes: Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index (WOSI), American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, Rowe score, range of motion, recurrence rates, apprehension, pain requiring injection, graft resorption on CT scan
articles.take_home: Among rugby players who had both procedures on opposite shoulders, the Bristow procedure produced better functional outcomes and symptom control compared to the Latarjet procedure. The Bristow side had no recurrence of instability, whereas the Latarjet side had two cases of subluxation and showed more graft loss on imaging.

articles.title: Glenoid Dysplasia is Associated with Acromial Dysplasia.
articles.authors: Levene S, Arroyo RA, Byrne RA, Joyce CD, Tashjian RZ, Chalmers PN
articles.population: Patients with glenoid dysplasia compared to controls without glenoid dysplasia
articles.sample_size: 18 patients with glenoid dysplasia and 100 controls
articles.outcomes: Measurements of glenoid retroversion, superior inclination, acromial width, acromial tilt, acromial coverage, and scapular spine angle
articles.take_home: Patients with glenoid dysplasia have significant differences in both shoulder socket and acromion (shoulder blade tip) anatomy, suggesting the problem affects the whole shoulder blade rather than just the socket. These findings may help guide surgical planning for patients with this condition.

articles.title: Prevalence, progression and factors associated with contralateral rotator cuff tears in patients treated for unilateral symptomatic non-traumatic rotator cuff tears: A scoping review.
articles.authors: Littlewood C, Moffatt M, Winter A, Lalande T, Rees J, Smith T
articles.population: Adults with unilateral symptomatic non-traumatic rotator cuff tears
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of contralateral rotator cuff tears (8.7% to 67.3%), tear enlargement (39% to 67%), contralateral shoulder pain development (26% to 57%), time to tear enlargement (2.8 to 3.4 years median), time to symptom onset (15.2 months to 3.0 years)
articles.take_home: People with a rotator cuff tear in one shoulder commonly develop tears in the other shoulder, which often enlarge over time. Risk factors include older age, higher BMI, diabetes, heavy repetitive work, and muscle degeneration in the unaffected shoulder.

articles.title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: Management of Periprosthetic Shoulder Infection.
articles.authors: Namdari S, Zmistowski B, Fiandeiro M, Gupta S, Nicholson T
articles.study_type: International consensus meeting using modified Delphi process
articles.population: International shoulder surgeons, infectious disease physicians, and microbiology experts
articles.outcomes: 13 questions resulted in clinical practice recommendations; 16 identified need for further research. All achieved supermajority consensus (92-100% agreement). Recommendations covered antimicrobial strategies, antibiotic cement, spacer types, implant removal, and component exchange approaches.
articles.take_home: Experts agreed on several approaches to treating infected shoulder replacements, including using intravenous or oral antibiotics tailored to the infection, removing modular components during surgery when possible, and removing well-fixed glenoid components in certain cases. However, significant gaps in evidence remain and more high-quality research is needed to establish the best treatment strategies.

articles.title: The Lateralization and Distalization Shoulder Angles in Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty Are Highly Sensitive to Both Arm Position and Viewing Angle: Analyzed Using the Enovis Altivate and Surgicase.
articles.authors: Kane LT, Namdari S, Amini M
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty without glenoid bone loss
articles.outcomes: Lateralization shoulder angle (LSA), distalization shoulder angle (DSA), acromiohumeral interval (AHI), and distance from glenosphere centre of rotation to greater tuberosity (GT-COR)
articles.take_home: Measurements commonly used to assess reverse shoulder replacement implant position (LSA and DSA) are unreliable as they vary significantly depending on how the arm is positioned and the angle of the X-ray image. Linear measurements of implant position are more stable and less affected by these variations.

articles.title: The 'Lower-Trap-Door' technique: Inlay trapezoidal Achilles bone-block fixation for lower trapezius tendon transfer.
articles.study_type: Technical note describing a novel surgical technique
articles.population: Patients undergoing lower trapezius tendon transfer
articles.outcomes: No failures at the humeral bone-block interface observed; formal clinical outcome data not presented
articles.take_home: This is a new surgical technique for repairing shoulder problems by moving the lower trapezius tendon using a specially designed bone block. Early results show the technique appears reliable, but formal testing and larger studies are needed to confirm how well it works compared to other methods.

articles.title: Surgical Treatment of Trans-ulnar Basal Coronoid Fracture-Dislocations: Clinical and Radiographic Outcomes in 34 Patients at a Mean 4-Year Follow-up.
articles.authors: Marinelli A, Riva M, Coliva F, Villari E, Brunello V, Guerra E
articles.population: Patients with trans-ulnar basal coronoid fracture-dislocations treated surgically
articles.outcomes: Elbow range of motion, Mayo Elbow Performance Score, Broberg and Morrey score, QuickDASH, Single Assessment Numeric Evaluation, fracture healing, complications
articles.take_home: Most patients achieved good functional results after surgery for this complex elbow injury, with over 90% having good or excellent outcomes. However, complication rates were substantial at 44%, and patients with more fragmented coronoid fractures had poorer results.

articles.title: Clinical and Radiographic Outcomes of Suture Anchor Repair versus Transarticular Kirschner Wire Fixation of the Acromioclavicular Joint in Acute High-grade Dislocation: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.authors: Hirunthanawiwat T, Benjawongsathien K, Sutthapakti B, Reingrittha P, Larpjitkusol P, Laoruengthana A
articles.population: Patients with acute high-grade acromioclavicular joint dislocation
articles.outcomes: Constant-Murley Score, American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, UCLA shoulder score, coracoclavicular distance change, and complications at 4, 8, 16, 24, and 52 weeks
articles.take_home: Suture anchor repair allowed faster early recovery with better function at 4-16 weeks, whilst K-wire fixation maintained better radiographic alignment. Both methods produced similar functional results by 24 weeks onwards, though K-wire fixation had a 25% complication rate including pin migration.

articles.title: Subscapularis Healing and the Associated Impact on Outcomes Following Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kevin Sungwook Lee AL, Rohl MR, Moor M, Baessler AM, Stephens SP, Badman BL
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with prospectively collected data
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary lateralised reverse shoulder arthroplasty with subscapularis repair
articles.outcomes: Subscapularis healing status on ultrasound, pain (VAS), function (ASES and SST scores), range of motion, strength, and complications at minimum 1 year follow-up
articles.take_home: Most subscapularis repairs healed after reverse shoulder surgery (79%), and healed repairs showed slightly better internal rotation at one year and lower pain levels, though these differences were small. Healing was not independently linked to overall shoulder movement after accounting for other factors.

articles.title: The Latarjet with Anterior Capsular Shift for Anterior Shoulder Instability in Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome: A Case Series.
articles.authors: Bailey EP, Sullivan CM, Hardrick JC, Seilern Und Aspang J, Grundman H, Wagner ER
articles.population: Patients with hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome and anterior-predominant shoulder instability
articles.outcomes: Recurrent shoulder instability, range of motion, pain (VAS), shoulder function (SSV and ASES scores), and complications
articles.take_home: In this small case series, the Latarjet procedure with anterior capsular shift prevented recurrent shoulder instability in all patients with hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, with significant improvements in pain and shoulder function. One patient had a graft fracture requiring revision surgery, but no cases of instability recurrence were reported.

articles.title: Prior Clostridioides difficile Infection Is Associated with Infectious Complications Following Total Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Paul BR, Patel JR, Moore ML, Hassebrock JD, Tokish JM, Deckey DG
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national claims database with propensity score matching
articles.sample_size: 782 patients with prior Clostridioides difficile infection matched 1:4 to 3,098 controls
articles.outcomes: Two-year periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) rates; subsequent CDI; pneumonia, sepsis, urinary tract infection, and hospital admission
articles.take_home: Patients who had a Clostridioides difficile infection before shoulder replacement surgery had a higher risk of developing a joint infection after surgery, especially if the infection occurred within three months before the operation. These patients also had a much higher risk of getting another Clostridioides difficile infection afterwards.

articles.title: CT-Based Morphology and Outcomes After ORIF of Humeral Head Articular Fractures.
articles.authors: Gavaskar AS, Ayyadurai P, Srinivasan P, Tummala NC
articles.population: Patients with articular fractures of the humeral head treated with open reduction and internal fixation
articles.outcomes: Union rates, functional scores (Constant score and QuickDASH), reduction quality, avascular necrosis incidence, complications and reoperations at mean 62 months follow-up
articles.take_home: Most humeral head fractures healed well after surgery with acceptable function, but more complex fractures (types 3-5) had poorer results, more bone death, and less chance of good healing. If surgery failed, conversion to shoulder replacement improved function significantly.

articles.title: Propensity-Matched Comparison of Stemless and Stemmed Anatomic Total Shoulder Arthroplasty in Patients Over 70 Years of Age.
articles.authors: Abdelshaheed J, Beleckas CM, Garcia JR, Obeid T, Grand ZA, Chatterji R, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort comparison with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients aged 70 years and over with glenohumeral osteoarthritis and intact rotator cuff undergoing primary anatomic total shoulder replacement
articles.outcomes: American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, Simple Shoulder Test, pain and function scores, range of motion, patient satisfaction, radiographic evidence of component loosening and bone resorption
articles.take_home: Stemless shoulder replacements performed as well as traditional stemmed replacements in patients over 70, with similar excellent clinical outcomes and high patient satisfaction at two years. Stemless replacements showed some radiographic advantages with less glenoid loosening and bone loss around the shoulder socket.

articles.title: Surgical versus non-surgical treatment for metacarpal shaft fractures : a prospective feasibility study.
articles.authors: Taha R, Leighton P, Davis T, Montgomery A, Karantana A, Murray A, et al.
articles.study_type: Prospective multicentre feasibility study with embedded qualitative research
articles.population: Adults aged 16 years and over with acute displaced metacarpal shaft fractures
articles.sample_size: 201 eligible patients; 108 recruited (median age 32 years, 68% male)
articles.outcomes: Grip strength, range of motion, radiological parameters, QuickDASH, PROMIS-UE, EQ-5D-5L, and Global Rating of Change measured at six weeks, three months, and six months
articles.take_home: A full randomised trial comparing surgery and non-surgery for hand fractures is feasible and patients found the proposed questionnaires and follow-up schedule acceptable. However, researchers will need better strategies to keep patients engaged beyond six weeks, as only 45% attended the six-month assessment.

articles.title: Do we classify and treat consistently? A retrospective, two-centre observer agreement study of Neer classification and treatment selection for proximal humerus fractures.
articles.authors: Palafox Carral I, Goinikman Braverman J, Colin Lara X, Rivero Celaya BO
articles.outcomes: Interobserver and intraobserver agreement for Neer classification; association between Neer category and treatment recommendation; factors associated with treatment selection
articles.take_home: The Neer classification system for shoulder fractures showed only moderate consistency when different doctors classified the same fractures, but the classification did influence whether doctors chose surgery or not. Older patients were much more likely to be recommended for joint replacement rather than repair surgery.

articles.title: Reverse shoulder arthroplasty after failed tendon transfer: A systematic review of clinical outcomes and complications from the FP-UCBM shoulder study group.
articles.authors: De Rosa A, Cardinale ME, Paciotti M, Franceschetti E, Ciuffreda M, Di Fabio S, et al.
articles.population: Patients who had reverse shoulder arthroplasty after a failed or symptomatic tendon transfer for massive irreparable rotator cuff tears
articles.sample_size: 77 tendon transfers (70 shoulders with transfer-specific outcome data) across 5 included studies
articles.outcomes: Pain reduction, forward elevation, Constant score, ASES score, external rotation, internal rotation, complications, reoperations and revisions
articles.take_home: Reverse shoulder arthroplasty after failed tendon transfer effectively reduces pain and restores the ability to lift the arm forwards, but patients experience more complications and need for further surgery compared to primary reverse shoulder surgery, and rotational movement is rarely restored.
